subject: abs vs. fabs; auto-casting real to int is dangerous

messages.author: e531efa2753b204e
messages.subject: abs vs. fabs; auto-casting real to int is dangerous
parts:
I just literally spent two days tracking down why posterior predictions in my model were not what a parallel computation in R thought they should be.

Turns out abs(real x) actually computes floor(abs(x)) because "abs" is for integers and "fabs" is for floats and, "abs" on a real value apparently casts to int first.

This is bizarre. I can tolerate there being different functions for integer and float, but in that case it should be an error to call abs() on a real value. For it to auto-cast to int is asking for problems.

Can there be some documentation in the User's guide on the difference between abs(real x) and fabs(real x)?

Better yet, can there be better behavior when auto-casting (such as warning when implicit real->int casts discard fractional parts?)

Peter

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] abs vs. fabs; auto-casting real to int is dangerous
parts:
On 10/4/13 10:38 PM, Peter Meilstrup wrote:
> I just literally spent two days tracking down why posterior predictions in my model were not what a parallel computation
> in R thought they should be.

I'm truly sorry to hear that. Thanks so much for reporting this calmly
and not yelling at us.

> Turns out abs(real x) actually computes floor(abs(x)) because "abs" is for integers and "fabs" is for floats and, "abs"
> on a real value apparently casts to int first.
This is a bug, not our intention.

> This is bizarre. I can tolerate there being different functions for integer and float, but in that case it should be an
> error to call abs() on a real value. For it to auto-cast to int is asking for problems.

I agree. The problem is that C++ is bringing in the
standard library definition of abs(int) and applying it
by casting the double to an int. Our implementation will
do the right thing for parameter real, just not data real
values.
> Can there be some documentation in the User's guide on the difference between abs(real x) and fabs(real x)?

> Better yet, can there be better behavior when auto-casting (such as warning when implicit real->int casts discard
> fractional parts?)

Yes. The current behavior's a bug as is the current doc
for not at least indicating our intention that abs(real) and
fabs(real) do the same thing.

I created a simple replicable example of the bug and included
it in the issue I just put in our issue tracker:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/257

This is very high priority and will definitely go in before 2.0.

I'm torn between the two solutions listed in the issue:

1. Try to get abs(real) do the same thing as fabs(real).

2. Remove abs(real) altogether.

I like 2 better, but I worry about backward compatiblity.

Best is probably:

3. Follow (1) and at same time deprecate use of abs(real)

- Bob
